narrative_purpose: Anchors the cold open: shows that every load-bearing surface of the village — roots, seawall, lagoon floor — is biological, not geological.
subject: A cutaway side view of a Metkayina dwelling cluster and the reef beneath it. At the top, a woven pod-dwelling hangs from the thick arching aerial roots of a giant mangrove-like tree. The roots plunge into clear water and spread into a dense living root matrix. Below, the seabed is a pale accreted limestone-like platform riddled with cavities, its living upper surface carpeted with branching and massive coral-analogue colonies. To one side, a low cascading terraced seawall rises in stepped rimmed pools.
scene: A shallow reef lagoon shown in vertical cross-section from air above to reef floor below, calm water, a few fish among the coral.
camera: Straight-on side elevation, layered top-to-bottom: dwelling, roots, water column, living reef floor.
light: Cool teal water light, cyan glow along the living coral rim and root tips, dim indigo in the deeper cavities, faint warm accent in the dwelling.
palette: Ocean teal and void indigo, cyan living-edge glow, one small warm amber dwelling accent.
style: Painterly naturalist cross-section plate, observed field-illustration energy.
detail_level: Crisp on the root matrix and the living-vs-accreted reef boundary; open low-detail water for overlay labels.
composition: Clear vertical stack with open dark water on the left margin for callouts, structure banked to the right.
consistency_notes: Dwelling hangs from LIVING roots; the seabed shows a clear boundary between living coral veneer on top and pale accreted framework below. Keep the same reef palette as the cover.
